domain_restrictions: a, b, and m are integers.
The ring Lambda_b is a polynomial algebra over the rationals in b generators.
The generator e_i has degree i for each i from 1 to b.
The family h_t is indexed by nonnegative integers t.
The quotient ideal is generated by the first a generators, so it is homogeneous.
The Hilbert series is taken with respect to the grading by degree.
If a = b, the product from i = a + 1 to b is empty and is interpreted as 1.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers a, b, and m with 0 <= a <= b and m >= 0, if Lambda_b is the graded polynomial ring over the rationals on generators e_1 through e_b with deg(e_i) = i and e_0 = 1, and if h_t for t >= 0 are defined by the generating-series identity, then the quotient ring R_{a,b} by the ideal generated by e_1 through e_a is a positively graded rational algebra with finite-dimensional graded pieces, its Hilbert series is the reciprocal of the product of 1 minus q raised to i for i from a + 1 to b, and the image of h_m in the quotient is homogeneous of degree m.
quantifier_order: Choose integers a, b, and m with 0 <= a <= b and m >= 0.
Define the graded polynomial ring Lambda_b over the rationals on generators e_1 through e_b, with deg(e_i) = i and e_0 = 1.
For each nonnegative integer t, define h_t in Lambda_b by the generating-series identity involving the e_i and the formal variable z.
Form the quotient ring R_{a,b} by the ideal generated by e_1 through e_a.
Let bar h_m be the image of h_m in R_{a,b}.
Assert that R_{a,b} has the stated grading properties, Hilbert series formula, and that bar h_m has degree m.

witness_dependencies: The elements h_t are not independent choices; they are determined by the generators e_1 through e_b and the convention e_0 = 1 through the generating-series identity.
The class bar h_m depends on the choice of m and on the quotient map from Lambda_b to R_{a,b}.
The Hilbert series formula depends on the grading deg(e_i) = i and on quotienting by the ideal generated by e_1 through e_a.
The statement that bar h_m has degree m depends on h_m being homogeneous of degree m in Lambda_b and on the quotient map preserving the grading.

statement_nl: Let a, b, and m be integers with 0 <= a <= b and m >= 0. Define the graded polynomial ring Lambda_b := Q[e_1,...,e_b] with deg(e_i) = i, let R_{a,b} := Lambda_b/(e_1,...,e_a), and define elements h_t in Lambda_b for t >= 0 by the generating-series identity (sum_{i=0}^b (-1)^i e_i z^i)(sum_{t>=0} h_t z^t) = 1, where e_0 := 1. Let bar h_m denote the image of h_m in R_{a,b}. Then R_{a,b} is a positively graded Q-algebra with finite-dimensional graded pieces, Hilb(R_{a,b};q) = 1 / product_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^i), and bar h_m is homogeneous of degree m.
